title: Lightweight GPU/CPU occupancy counters and perf-dashboard exporter for microbench harness
author: Evan Holt
release_notes:
Adds low-overhead occupancy counters for CPU/GPU execution paths plus a lightweight exporter that uploads aggregated microbench metrics to the internal perf-dashboard. No runtime behavior changes; telemetry-only.
- New counters for kernel occupancy, queue-depth, and batching latency buckets.
- Speeds up root-cause of tail-latency regressions while keeping overhead <0.5% on production traces.
description: Context and motivation: We've had recurring uncertainty about whether tail latency spikes are due to kernel launch contention, GPU multiprocessor occupancy, or runtime queueing pressure. Existing NVTX ranges and high-res timers (previous PRs) are useful but expensive to keep enabled across long microbench runs. This PR introduces a set of low-overhead, sample-based occupancy counters on both CPU and GPU hotpaths plus a tiny exporter that aggregates per-microbench histograms and posts them to the internal perf-dashboard. Summary of changes: 1) instrumentation: new occ_counters module with lock-free incrementers, per-thread sampling, and a compact on-device GPU occupancy probe that reads SM occupancy counters exposed by CUDA via cupti-lite. 2) exporter: occ_exporter collects interval histograms, computes p50/p95/p99 and heatmap buckets, signs and uploads via existing dashboard ingestion API. 3) microbench integration: runner_perf.py hooks to enable counters for a run and emit an occurrence manifest for dashboard indexing. 4) docs and examples plus CI perf-check that validates exporter end-to-end against a synthetic run. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4217) - [x] Microbench integration smoke tests - [x] Dashboard ingestion adapter implemented and tested - [x] Perf CI step added to validate no regressions in overhead - [x] Security review for exporter endpoint (no secrets baked in) Commits (high-level): - Add occ_counters module and header, sampling strategy and unit tests (5 commits) - Add occ_exporter and dashboard adapter with retries and backoff (3 commits) - Integrate runner_perf and example trace (2 commits) - Docs and CI changes (2 commits) Files changed (high-level): - runtime/src/instrumentation/occ_counters.cpp: core counter implementations, light-weight sampling loop and atomic histograms - runtime/telemetry/occ_exporter.*: interval aggregation, JSON envelope and upload client, backoff - tools/microbench/runner_perf.py: new --enable-occ flag and local aggregation mode - observed changes to CMakeLists and dashboard adapter to wire the new module Review conversation (high-level): - Priya: "Can we guarantee the occupancy probe doesn't introduce device synchronizations? If not, what are the fallback paths?" Evan: "The probe reads CUPTI lightweight counters asynchronously; we pin to the non-blocking API path and fall back to a best-effort sampler that only reads a cached counter snapshot. Added unit test to detect inadvertent syncs (see occ_counters_sync_test)." - Jonas: "Consider exposing per-model tags in the exported payload so we can correlate with rollout metadata." Evan: "Added model_tag field and updated runner_perf to populate it from microbench config." - Lena: "CI flaky on perf-checks.yml in first run, failure was a timeout on synthetic ingest; re-ran and it passed. Please note tests are noisy on low-resource builders." Evan: "Noted, added a retry and increased timeout in the CI job." CI summary: perf-checks.yml runs a synthetic microbench that exercises sampling, exporter and dashboard ingest. First run showed a transient timeout on the ingest endpoint; after increasing timeout and adding a retry the job passes consistently on our builders. Local benchmark overhead: measured avg CPU overhead 0.18% (±0.05), GPU-side instrumentation measured at <0.5% for microbench traces with 4 concurrent streams. Compatibility notes: This is telemetry-only. If CUPTI is not present the watchdog falls back to kernel-launch counters and documented no-opers; behavior remains functionally identical. Security: exporter uses existing dashboard ingestion auth flow; no new keys embedded. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag OCC_COUNTERS_ENABLED (disabled by default in production). We'll enable for the perf lab and a small canary fleet for two weeks before turning on for full microbench CI. Merge outcome: squash-merged after approvals from Priya and Jonas and CI green. Follow-ups: 1) Add dashboard heatmap drilldown UI (ENG-4220) 2) Expand GPU occupancy probe to support A100 power islands (work queued).
